quests.sentence: I've finished the report, so we can start the meeting whenever you're ready.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have finished is the present perfect form, connecting a completed action to its usefulness right now.
quests.nativeTip: The exact time of finishing doesn't matter here — what matters is that it's done now.
quests.example: I've finished the report, so we can start the meeting whenever you're ready.

quests.sentence: I finished the report at 4 p.m. yesterday.
quests.ruleExplanation: Finished is the simple past form, used because a specific past time is stated.
quests.nativeTip: Notice the specific, named time here — that changes what's needed compared to the previous sentence.
quests.example: I finished the report at 4 p.m. yesterday.

quests.sentence: She's already sent the invoices to the client.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has sent is the present perfect form, and already emphasizes that the task is done before now.
quests.nativeTip: 'Already' signals something completed with relevance to the current situation.
quests.example: She's already sent the invoices to the client.

quests.sentence: Have you ever tried Ethiopian food?
quests.ruleExplanation: Have tried is the present perfect form, used to ask about life experience up to now.
quests.nativeTip: This asks about experience at any point in life, not one specific occasion.
quests.example: Have you ever tried Ethiopian food?

quests.sentence: I've never been to Iceland, but it's on my list.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have been is the present perfect form, and never describes an experience that hasn't happened up to now.
quests.nativeTip: This is about experience across her whole life so far, not a single trip.
quests.example: I've never been to Iceland, but it's on my list.

quests.sentence: I went to Iceland for a wedding two summers ago.
quests.ruleExplanation: Went is the simple past form, used because the sentence refers to one specific completed event.
quests.nativeTip: This names a specific, finished trip rather than talking about experience in general.
quests.example: I went to Iceland for a wedding two summers ago.

quests.sentence: The plane has just landed.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has landed is the present perfect form, and just shows the action finished only moments ago.
quests.nativeTip: 'Just' points to something completed a very short moment ago.
quests.example: The plane has just landed.

quests.sentence: I haven't received the confirmation email yet.
quests.ruleExplanation: Haven't received is the negative present perfect form, and yet signals it still hasn't happened.
quests.nativeTip: 'Yet' shows something expected hasn't happened up to this point.
quests.example: I haven't received the confirmation email yet.

quests.sentence: Has the technician arrived yet?
quests.ruleExplanation: Has arrived is the present perfect form, used with yet to ask about an anticipated event.
quests.nativeTip: This question checks whether something expected has happened by now.
quests.example: Has the technician arrived yet?

quests.sentence: I've worked at this company for six years.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have worked is the present perfect form, and for six years measures a duration continuing up to now.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a situation that started in the past and is still true now.
quests.example: I've worked at this company for six years.

quests.sentence: We've known each other since college.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have known is the present perfect form, and since college marks the starting point of a situation that continues now.
quests.nativeTip: The friendship started at a past point and continues into the present.
quests.example: We've known each other since college.

quests.sentence: I worked at my previous company for four years before switching.
quests.ruleExplanation: Worked is the simple past form, describing a finished period of employment that has ended.
quests.nativeTip: This job is over — the situation no longer continues into the present.
quests.example: I worked at my previous company for four years before switching.

quests.sentence: I've read three books this month.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have read is the present perfect form, used because 'this month' is a time period still in progress.
quests.nativeTip: The month named in the sentence hasn't ended yet.
quests.example: I've read three books this month.

quests.sentence: I read two books last month.
quests.ruleExplanation: Read is the simple past form, used because the time period referred to has already ended.
quests.nativeTip: 'Last month' is a finished period of time.
quests.example: I read two books last month.

quests.sentence: Have you called the landlord this morning?
quests.ruleExplanation: Have called is the present perfect form, fitting an unfinished time period like 'this morning'.
quests.nativeTip: The morning mentioned is treated as a period that hasn't fully finished.
quests.example: Have you called the landlord this morning?

quests.sentence: Someone has left the back door open.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has left is the present perfect form, focusing on a present result rather than the specific moment it happened.
quests.nativeTip: What matters here is the current result, not who did it or exactly when.
quests.example: Someone has left the back door open.

quests.sentence: The manager left the office an hour ago.
quests.ruleExplanation: Left is the simple past form, used because a precise past time is given.
quests.nativeTip: A specific, known time is the key detail to notice here.
quests.example: The manager left the office an hour ago.

quests.sentence: The printer has broken down again.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has broken down is the present perfect form, describing a recent event still affecting the present situation.
quests.nativeTip: 'Again' hints at a recurring problem that's currently affecting things.
quests.example: The printer has broken down again.

quests.sentence: Prices have risen sharply since the pandemic.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have risen is the present perfect form, describing a change that began in the past and continues to affect the present.
quests.nativeTip: This change started in the past and is still true today.
quests.example: Prices have risen sharply since the pandemic.

quests.sentence: The city's population grew by ten percent last decade.
quests.ruleExplanation: Grew is the simple past form, describing a change confined to a completed period of time.
quests.nativeTip: 'Last decade' refers to a finished period that has ended.
quests.example: The city's population grew by ten percent last decade.

quests.sentence: Technology has improved dramatically in the past ten years.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has improved is the present perfect form, describing a change over a period that extends up to the present.
quests.nativeTip: This describes an ongoing trend that includes right now.
quests.example: Technology has improved dramatically in the past ten years.

quests.sentence: I haven't slept well lately.
quests.ruleExplanation: Haven't slept is the negative present perfect form, and lately signals a recent pattern affecting the present.
quests.nativeTip: 'Lately' points to a recent stretch of time connected to now.
quests.example: I haven't slept well lately.

quests.sentence: She's been quieter than usual recently.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has been is the present perfect form of be, describing a recent and ongoing change in behavior.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a recent state that's still noticeable now.
quests.example: She's been quieter than usual recently.

quests.sentence: We recently moved to a new office downtown.
quests.ruleExplanation: Moved is the simple past form; recently can describe a specific completed action, not only present perfect situations.
quests.nativeTip: Even with the word 'recently', this describes one completed move, not an ongoing situation.
quests.example: We recently moved to a new office downtown.

quests.sentence: I saw that movie last week.
quests.ruleExplanation: Saw is the simple past form, used because a specific past time is mentioned.
quests.nativeTip: Pay attention to the specific named time in this sentence.
quests.example: I saw that movie last week.

quests.sentence: I've seen that movie already.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have seen is the present perfect form, used when the exact time doesn't matter, only that the experience has occurred.
quests.nativeTip: No specific time is given — what matters is that it's already happened.
quests.example: I've seen that movie already.

quests.sentence: I haven't finished the assignment yet, but I will by tonight.
quests.ruleExplanation: Haven't finished is the negative present perfect form, showing the task remains incomplete as of now.
quests.nativeTip: This describes something still incomplete up to the present moment.
quests.example: I haven't finished the assignment yet, but I will by tonight.

quests.sentence: The negotiations have reached a critical stage.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have reached is the present perfect form, describing a development that is directly relevant to the present situation.
quests.nativeTip: There's no obvious keyword here — think about whether this is a finished historical event or a current situation.
quests.example: The negotiations have reached a critical stage.

quests.sentence: The negotiations have dragged on for three months with no resolution in sight.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have dragged on is the present perfect form, describing a duration that continues up to now.
quests.nativeTip: This situation started in the past and is still ongoing.
quests.example: The negotiations have dragged on for three months with no resolution in sight.

quests.sentence: Talks broke down completely last spring, ending years of cooperation.
quests.ruleExplanation: Broke down is the simple past form, describing a completed event from a specific past time.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a finished historical event with no stated connection to the present.
quests.example: Talks broke down completely last spring, ending years of cooperation.
